questions.prompt: Is a microservice boundary primarily an architectural or a deployment decision?

options.text: Primarily a deployment/operational decision — physical separation doesn't guarantee architectural independence
Primarily an architectural decision that guarantees decoupling
It's the same as the Dependency Rule

questions.explanation: A service boundary is about how the system is deployed and operated. Services can still be tightly coupled through shared data and cross-cutting features.

options.text: That services are always slower than a monolith
The belief that splitting into services automatically yields decoupling and independent development
That services must share a database

questions.explanation: Shared data and cross-cutting features can still force coordinated changes across services, so 'we used microservices' doesn't by itself mean the system is decoupled.

questions.prompt: Many services sharing one database and calling each other for every request, so features need coordinated cross-service changes, is derisively called a distributed ______.
questions.explanation: A distributed monolith has all the costs of services with none of the independence, because shared data and chatty contracts recouple the services.

questions.prompt: Match each decoupling mode to its description.

pairs.right: Separate processes communicating over a network

questions.explanation: A microservice is decoupling pushed to the service level — the strongest and most expensive form of the boundary spectrum.

questions.prompt: Which are genuine costs that the service level adds over in-process decoupling? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Services add network, consistency, and operational costs. They do NOT provide automatic architectural decoupling — that still requires good design.

questions.prompt: Order the 'monolith-first' steps for arriving at a well-justified service.

items.text: Build a modular monolith with clean internal boundaries
Identify a concrete force on one module (e.g., independent scaling)
Extract that module as a separate service
Connect it via a driving adapter (endpoint) and its own driven adapter (store)

questions.explanation: Start with a modular monolith and extract a service only when a real force appears; the extracted service's endpoint becomes a driving adapter and its database a driven adapter, with entities and use cases inside.
